name: Plan pipeline
description: Turns a feature request into four reviewed documents under docs/plans/<feature>/: the Analyst clarifies the requirements with the operator and writes PRD.md, the Scout checks them against the codebase, the Architect writes ARCHITECTURE.md (operator approves the design), the Planner slices TASKS.md into tickets and WAVES.md into waves (operator approves the plan), and the Integrator commits the documents in one merge request and publishes the tickets as tracker issues, one per ticket, grouped in waves.

task.description: The feature, as the requester states it

feature.description: Slug naming the feature; the documents go to docs/plans/<feature>/

nodes.task:
Review the PRD at {{.state.analyst.prd_path}} against the code in the checkout for the feature {{.input.feature}}.

Read the code the requirements touch. Find where the PRD contradicts the code, assumes something that does not exist, or leaves out something the code forces (gaps), and the facts a designer must respect: language and toolchain, how to build and run the tests, conventions, modules the feature must extend (constraints). Run the build and the test suite once to confirm the commands work. Save the build and test commands and any lasting convention as project notes with memory_save (scope project). Do not edit files and leave no build outputs in the repository: build in a scratch directory outside the checkout, or remove any untracked file your build or tests created before finishing. Finish with gaps and constraints, each a list of short sentences.

Slice the feature {{.input.feature}} into tickets. Read docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}/PRD.md and docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}/ARCHITECTURE.md.

Each ticket is one thin end-to-end slice (a tracer bullet through every layer it needs) that one builder can finish and review alone, with its own acceptance tests; the first ticket is the thinnest working path. Write docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}/TASKS.md with, per ticket: id, title, the slice, the files it creates or changes, and the acceptance tests. Ids are T<n>, unique across the feature and without a wave prefix (T1, T2, T3...); which wave a ticket is built in is decided next, in WAVES.md. List every file path a ticket touches in files; tickets that touch the same file will be put in different waves.
{{with .state.plan_gate}}{{if eq .decision "rejected"}}
The operator rejected the previous plan.{{if .reason}} Reason:
{{.reason}}
{{end}} Revise docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}/TASKS.md to address it before finishing.
{{end}}{{end}}Finish with tickets: a list of {id, title, slice, files, tests}: slice is the end-to-end slice as written in TASKS.md (a sentence or two; it becomes the issue text), files the paths it touches, tests the acceptance tests as a list of strings (each a test name or a one-line check).

Group the tickets of {{.input.feature}} into waves and write docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}/WAVES.md.

A wave is a set of tickets built in parallel; the next wave starts when the previous one is merged. Number waves from 1 without gaps. Put every ticket in exactly one wave, a ticket after the tickets it depends on, and never two tickets that list a common file in the same wave. WAVES.md gives each wave's goal, its tickets and why they can run in parallel. A finish that breaks these rules is refused with the reason. Finish with waves: a list of {n, tickets: [ticket id]}.

Publish the approved plan of {{.input.feature}} in two steps. The four documents docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}/PRD.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, TASKS.md and WAVES.md are in the checkout.

1. Open one merge request with the open_merge_request tool with paths ["docs/plans/{{.input.feature}}"], so it commits only that directory and nothing else left in the checkout: title "Plan: {{.input.feature}}", description with the PRD summary ({{.state.analyst.summary}}) and the waves. Do not change the documents.
2. Then call the publish_tickets tool with your run_token and nothing else. It reads the approved tickets and waves from the run itself and creates one tracker issue per ticket; do not try to create issues any other way.

If either tool result says the action was rejected or is pending approval, finish with empty merge_request_url and plan_id and issues_count 0. Otherwise finish with merge_request_url from the first tool, plan_id and issues_count (the number of issues) from the second.
